plan: Second-price sealed-bid auctions make truthful bidding a weakly dominant strategy. With value 49 (the maximum), bidding my true value maximizes expected profit: I win unless tied at 49, and I pay the second-highest bid. Overbidding risks negative profit if opponents deviate; underbidding risks losing when profitable. With no informative history and one round, truth-telling is optimal and safe, ensuring non-negative profit when winning.

Second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values. Dominant strategy: bid true value. With value $44 on [0,49], bidding 44 maximizes expected profit: it guarantees winning whenever our value is highest while paying the second-highest bid. Shading down risks losing profitable wins; bidding above value risks winning when price exceeds value (if others overbid), which can reduce expected profit. No history to exploit in this one-shot round, so follow the dominant strategy.

[ In a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. Overbidding risks winning at a price above value; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. With no history to exploit and value = 22, bid exactly 22. If we win (both others < 22), we pay the second-highest bid and earn 22 minus that price. ]
